requirements.obligation: Machines, belts, storage, defenses and vehicles visibly perform their actual function across idle/input/start/run/output/empty/full/blocked/damaged/destroyed/rebuilt/restart states. Rebuild the furnace at level1 with a substantial progression/lost-tier raw-material bill, then re-earn upgrades. Manual gathering, recovery jobs, salvage/cash collection, combat and construction remain possible. Show stock type/quantity, requested combination, actual costs, separate cash, worker intent, priority warning, damage severity, death, ruin, replacement and restoration. requirements.obligation: Implement the fourteen testable AI details in the actor contract: eligibility, stable priorities, shared reservations, safe preemption, player agency, route/target recovery, custody, fairness, survival awareness, truthful perception, save continuity, budgets and readable intent. Ordinary simulation pauses while backgrounded/closed. Scheduled raids require a full five-minute (300 active seconds) warning naming the threatened camp, with a saved 5:00 countdown, sound and equivalent muted cue; no scheduled-raid damage occurs before it expires. If admission is due while ineligible, wait and then give the full warning. This does not cancel real roaming threats.

requirements.title: Persistent loss, cargo and recovery integrity
requirements.obligation: Preserve authoritative cargo, purchase and recovery receipts through cancellation, defeat if designed, app suspension, crash, reconnect and migration; no duplicated payout/debit or repeated committed penalty. Current U3 additions: Repair plots quote materials appropriate to asset/tier and missing HP. A repair job has a fixed authorized HP/material budget; new damage cannot be erased for free. Fence/gate ruins may be reconstructed through the repair plot at their purchased tier. Uncommitted escrow returns safely when the asset generation changes. Non-boundary equipment at zero HP becomes a ruin. Rebuy through the appropriate plot using a new generation and level 1 equipment. Account progression and known recipes remain unlocked, but lost equipment upgrades must be purchased again. Persist destruction; cancel/refund only uncommitted work, not already consumed production or repairs. Pets and survivors can die. Death tombstones the live instance, cancels its attacks/jobs/reservations and requires an ordinary earnable-resource/cash replacement purchase. A new instance is created once; preserve earned companion level/XP/skills, account unlocks and permanent paid entitlements because the user only required equipment level resets. No free care revival or automatic respawn. Dead companion cargo and destroyed equipment/counter/storage contents move once into persistent typed salvage custody. Recovering that cache is a real reachable job. Already sold customer goods are no longer player stock and do not become resale loot on visitor death. All ownership remains single-valued across transitions. Retain permanent baseline player gathering capability and a reachable renewable manual wood/stone path. Recovery bills cannot require a destroyed producer, new customer payout, premium purchase or companion. A finite saved siege objective/attack budget ends in retreat after core defeat without a victory reward; scheduled new camp raids pause through reconstruction, while roaming threats remain real.

Use justified static/shared dispositions where appropriate; no generic placeholder masquerades as finished action. Current U3 additions: Latest U3 permits survivors to initiate eligible assigned hunts and attacks. Distinguish explicitly huntable wildlife, invaders, customers, companions and friendlies by identity/role rather than art. Owned pets are never prey. Attacking an enemy makes that survivor eligible for that enemy's retaliation. Pets and survivors can die. Death tombstones the live instance, cancels its attacks/jobs/reservations and requires an ordinary earnable-resource/cash replacement purchase. A new instance is created once; preserve earned companion level/XP/skills, account unlocks and permanent paid entitlements because the user only required equipment level resets. No free care revival or automatic respawn. Show stock type/quantity, requested combination, actual costs, separate cash, worker intent, priority warning, damage severity, death, ruin, replacement and restoration. Every interaction has applicable approach/contact/commit/blocked/cancel/recovery motion and sound; physical pickups and money placement correspond to real ledger changes.

Real-time and slow playback from distinct meaningful views

Assigned hunt with real tool/contact/cargo return
Retaliation after an initiated attack including a legitimate miss

requirements.title: Readable enemy and combat variety
requirements.obligation: Each introduced enemy/weapon/locomotion archetype has authored intent, tell, attack, hit/miss, recovery and response states, with visible range/timing matching damage and meaningful counterplay. Current U3 additions: Latest U3 permits survivors to initiate eligible assigned hunts and attacks. Distinguish explicitly huntable wildlife, invaders, customers, companions and friendlies by identity/role rather than art. Owned pets are never prey. Attacking an enemy makes that survivor eligible for that enemy's retaliation. While the player or an eligible living defending pet is within the camp's defense range, enemies target eligible reachable player/pet/camp objectives. An unprovoked survivor is ineligible as a direct target, including when every preferred target is absent or blocked. Seek a valid approach or blocking defense instead. An enemy may directly retaliate against the survivor that attacks it; both player and eligible defending pets being far permits unrestricted targets. This does not grant collateral damage immunity: an actual valid contact can still hurt a survivor. Fences and gates have substantial authored HP but can be breached. Every placed camp/field equipment class has HP and damaged/destroyed states. Breaches change collision and pathing at the actual commit. Interior safety comes from intact defenses, defenders and enemy behavior; standing inside camp is not permanent invulnerability.

GR02: Player and unlocked survivors share unlimited logical mixed raw, processed and ordinary-money custody. A worker can bulk collect cash and deposit it at a valid destination. Useful job amounts and destinations bound work; rendered pile count is not capacity.

GR03: New customer baskets may combine processed products from operating unlocked producers or genuinely reachable purchasable/rebuildable producer paths. Prove unlock, route, raw source, tool, recipe, plot bill, capacity and quantity dependencies without assuming this order's unearned payout. Mere ownership or a render is insufficient.

GR04: Material types, mix and quantities vary by authored progression band, target class/tier and accessible economy. No purchase/upgrade bill may depend solely on its own output or a descendant that it enables. Use attainable alternative materials or a bootstrap bill when recovery removes a producer.

GR05: Persist quote ID, generation, catalogue version, progression snapshot, item quantities, payout and committed contributions. Keep accepted/part-paid quotes stable through ordinary progression. Revalidate feasibility on material changes; cancel only uncommitted work with conserved escrow. Reject request-ID reuse with a different payload.

GR06: Latest U3 permits survivors to initiate eligible assigned hunts and attacks. Distinguish explicitly huntable wildlife, invaders, customers, companions and friendlies by identity/role rather than art. Owned pets are never prey. Attacking an enemy makes that survivor eligible for that enemy's retaliation.

GR10: Repair plots quote materials appropriate to asset/tier and missing HP. A repair job has a fixed authorized HP/material budget; new damage cannot be erased for free. Fence/gate ruins may be reconstructed through the repair plot at their purchased tier. Uncommitted escrow returns safely when the asset generation changes.

GR11: Non-boundary equipment at zero HP becomes a ruin. Rebuy through the appropriate plot using a new generation and level 1 equipment. Account progression and known recipes remain unlocked, but lost equipment upgrades must be purchased again. Persist destruction; cancel/refund only uncommitted work, not already consumed production or repairs.

GR12: Pets and survivors can die. Death tombstones the live instance, cancels its attacks/jobs/reservations and requires an ordinary earnable-resource/cash replacement purchase. A new instance is created once; preserve earned companion level/XP/skills, account unlocks and permanent paid entitlements because the user only required equipment level resets. No free care revival or automatic respawn.

GR13: Dead companion cargo and destroyed equipment/counter/storage contents move once into persistent typed salvage custody. Recovering that cache is a real reachable job. Already sold customer goods are no longer player stock and do not become resale loot on visitor death. All ownership remains single-valued across transitions.

GR14: Furnace destruction puts that camp into blackout: pause automated production, new customer admission and ordinary non-recovery worker jobs; preserve already committed value. Rebuild the furnace at level1 with a substantial progression/lost-tier raw-material bill, then re-earn upgrades. Manual gathering, recovery jobs, salvage/cash collection, combat and construction remain possible.

GR15: Retain permanent baseline player gathering capability and a reachable renewable manual wood/stone path. Recovery bills cannot require a destroyed producer, new customer payout, premium purchase or companion. A finite saved siege objective/attack budget ends in retreat after core defeat without a victory reward; scheduled new camp raids pause through reconstruction, while roaming threats remain real.

GR17: Migrate old saves preserving earned goods, existing companions/levels, quotes, purchases and paid entitlements. Remove only the obsolete attendant role; preserve customer identity assets. Introduce HP/death/generation ledgers without retroactive deaths or charging old completed work. Existing derived cash needs spent-outflow accounting before new spending.

GR18: Use progression, unlocked opportunity and selected equipment tier to author demand mixes, amounts, repair/replacement bills and encounter pressure. Do not price by current wallet size, paid history or VIP. Optional events do not repair a mandatory shortage. Preserve an achievable $0 route including repeated losses.

GR19: Run reusable native rule logic and adversarial transaction/recovery scenarios, then integrate it with the actual Godot scene, actors, persistence, navigation, contact events and art. Native headless rule tests do not certify 3D motion, actual physical contacts, all100 producer bindings, sound, physical devices or final reference quality.

GR20: Use latest U3 before U2/U1 where they conflict. Current user rules supersede earlier free repairs/free companion revival/permanent sanctuary and static service assumptions. Current task packets must project these rules without contradictory old instructions. Preserve historical audits, all70 task IDs/edges/owners, art and unresolved T71–T80 source gaps.

requirements.title: Readable stakes and bounded recovery
requirements.obligation: Define each threat warning, cause, consequence, exposure limit, counterplay, recovery, grace/repeat/offline behavior and save semantics. Apply the selected U3 loss policy explicitly; never present authored rules as observed footage or implemented scene behavior. Current U3 additions: While the player or an eligible living defending pet is within the camp's defense range, enemies target eligible reachable player/pet/camp objectives. Breaches change collision and pathing at the actual commit. Interior safety comes from intact defenses, defenders and enemy behavior; standing inside camp is not permanent invulnerability. Furnace destruction puts that camp into blackout: pause automated production, new customer admission and ordinary non-recovery worker jobs; preserve already committed value. Rebuild the furnace at level1 with a substantial progression/lost-tier raw-material bill, then re-earn upgrades. requirements.title: Readable stakes and bounded recovery
requirements.obligation: Define each threat warning, cause, consequence, exposure limit, counterplay, recovery, grace/repeat/offline behavior and save semantics. Apply the selected U3 loss policy explicitly; never present authored rules as observed footage or implemented scene behavior. Current U3 additions: While the player or an eligible living defending pet is within the camp's defense range, enemies target eligible reachable player/pet/camp objectives. An unprovoked survivor is ineligible as a direct target, including when every preferred target is absent or blocked. Seek a valid approach or blocking defense instead. An enemy may directly retaliate against the survivor that attacks it; both player and eligible defending pets being far permits unrestricted targets. This does not grant collateral damage immunity: an actual valid contact can still hurt a survivor. When both player and defending pets are beyond the warned defense boundary, hostile encounter policy permits all characters and destructible camp structures as targets. Manual gathering, recovery jobs, salvage/cash collection, combat and construction remain possible. Scheduled raids require a full five-minute (300 active seconds) warning naming the threatened camp, with a saved 5:00 countdown, sound and equivalent muted cue; no scheduled-raid damage occurs before it expires. requirements.title: Readable stakes and bounded recovery
requirements.obligation: Define each threat warning, cause, consequence, exposure limit, counterplay, recovery, grace/repeat/offline behavior and save semantics. Apply the selected U3 loss policy explicitly; never present authored rules as observed footage or implemented scene behavior. Current U3 additions: While the player or an eligible living defending pet is within the camp's defense range, enemies target eligible reachable player/pet/camp objectives. An unprovoked survivor is ineligible as a direct target, including when every preferred target is absent or blocked. Seek a valid approach or blocking defense instead. An enemy may directly retaliate against the survivor that attacks it; both player and eligible defending pets being far permits unrestricted targets. This does not grant collateral damage immunity: an actual valid contact can still hurt a survivor. When both player and defending pets are beyond the warned defense boundary, hostile encounter policy permits all characters and destructible camp structures as targets. Hysteresis stabilizes the boundary. Distance-based rendering or region unloading cannot delete the logical encounter, heal enemies or fabricate offscreen loot. Ordinary simulation pauses while backgrounded/closed. Fences and gates have substantial authored HP but can be breached. Every placed camp/field equipment class has HP and damaged/destroyed states. Breaches change collision and pathing at the actual commit. Interior safety comes from intact defenses, defenders and enemy behavior; standing inside camp is not permanent invulnerability. Furnace destruction puts that camp into blackout: pause automated production, new customer admission and ordinary non-recovery worker jobs; preserve already committed value. Rebuild the furnace at level1 with a substantial progression/lost-tier raw-material bill, then re-earn upgrades. Manual gathering, recovery jobs, salvage/cash collection, combat and construction remain possible. Scheduled raids require a full five-minute (300 active seconds) warning naming the threatened camp, with a saved 5:00 countdown, sound and equivalent muted cue; no scheduled-raid damage occurs before it expires. If admission is due while ineligible, wait and then give the full warning. This does not cancel real roaming threats.

requirements.title: Readable stakes and bounded recovery
requirements.obligation: Define each threat warning, cause, consequence, exposure limit, counterplay, recovery, grace/repeat/offline behavior and save semantics. Apply the selected U3 loss policy explicitly; never present authored rules as observed footage or implemented scene behavior. Current U3 additions: While the player or an eligible living defending pet is within the camp's defense range, enemies target eligible reachable player/pet/camp objectives. An unprovoked survivor is ineligible as a direct target, including when every preferred target is absent or blocked. Seek a valid approach or blocking defense instead. An enemy may directly retaliate against the survivor that attacks it; both player and eligible defending pets being far permits unrestricted targets. This does not grant collateral damage immunity: an actual valid contact can still hurt a survivor. When both player and defending pets are beyond the warned defense boundary, hostile encounter policy permits all characters and destructible camp structures as targets. Hysteresis stabilizes the boundary. Distance-based rendering or region unloading cannot delete the logical encounter, heal enemies or fabricate offscreen loot. Ordinary simulation pauses while backgrounded/closed. Fences and gates have substantial authored HP but can be breached. Every placed camp/field equipment class has HP and damaged/destroyed states. Breaches change collision and pathing at the actual commit. Interior safety comes from intact defenses, defenders and enemy behavior; standing inside camp is not permanent invulnerability. Furnace destruction puts that camp into blackout: pause automated production, new customer admission and ordinary non-recovery worker jobs; preserve already committed value. Rebuild the furnace at level1 with a substantial progression/lost-tier raw-material bill, then re-earn upgrades. Manual gathering, recovery jobs, salvage/cash collection, combat and construction remain possible. Scheduled raids require a full five-minute (300 active seconds) warning naming the threatened camp, with a saved 5:00 countdown, sound and equivalent muted cue; no scheduled-raid damage occurs before it expires. If admission is due while ineligible, wait and then give the full warning. This does not cancel real roaming threats.

requirements.title: Readable stakes and bounded recovery
requirements.obligation: Define each threat warning, cause, consequence, exposure limit, counterplay, recovery, grace/repeat/offline behavior and save semantics. Apply the selected U3 loss policy explicitly; never present authored rules as observed footage or implemented scene behavior. Current U3 additions: While the player or an eligible living defending pet is within the camp's defense range, enemies target eligible reachable player/pet/camp objectives. An unprovoked survivor is ineligible as a direct target, including when every preferred target is absent or blocked. Seek a valid approach or blocking defense instead. An enemy may directly retaliate against the survivor that attacks it; both player and eligible defending pets being far permits unrestricted targets. This does not grant collateral damage immunity: an actual valid contact can still hurt a survivor. When both player and defending pets are beyond the warned defense boundary, hostile encounter policy permits all characters and destructible camp structures as targets. Hysteresis stabilizes the boundary. Distance-based rendering or region unloading cannot delete the logical encounter, heal enemies or fabricate offscreen loot. Ordinary simulation pauses while backgrounded/closed. Fences and gates have substantial authored HP but can be breached. Every placed camp/field equipment class has HP and damaged/destroyed states. Breaches change collision and pathing at the actual commit. Interior safety comes from intact defenses, defenders and enemy behavior; standing inside camp is not permanent invulnerability. Furnace destruction puts that camp into blackout: pause automated production, new customer admission and ordinary non-recovery worker jobs; preserve already committed value. Rebuild the furnace at level1 with a substantial progression/lost-tier raw-material bill, then re-earn upgrades. Manual gathering, recovery jobs, salvage/cash collection, combat and construction remain possible. Scheduled raids require a full five-minute (300 active seconds) warning naming the threatened camp, with a saved 5:00 countdown, sound and equivalent muted cue; no scheduled-raid damage occurs before it expires. If admission is due while ineligible, wait and then give the full warning. This does not cancel real roaming threats.
